School of Software Engineering · Huazhong University of Science and Technology

Foundation Models & AI Agents

2025 AI Large Model Experimental Class · Second year · Spring 2027

Study the principles behind models that process language and images, then build an agent that uses models, tools, and evidence to complete a task.

Start with neural-network foundations and PyTorch, then study Transformers, language and vision models, and LLM agents. Four individual exercises prepare you for a concentrated two-week team project after the core lectures.

Theory course
32 hours · 2 credits
Project course
2 weeks · 2 credits
Prerequisites
Python, linear algebra, and basic probability
Team size
3 students

Course 01 · Theory

Core Principles & Frontier Applications of Large Models

Understand and implement core components: calculate attention, trace tensor shapes, explain training objectives, and use automatic differentiation. The opening four hours introduce neural-network training and PyTorch.

Course 02 · Practice

Large Models & AI Agents: Project Design

Teams of three choose different applications under common requirements. Integrate text and visual evidence, tools, state, and evaluation into a working agent.

Required work uses student laptops and teaching-provided language and vision APIs. No GPU is required. Prior neural-network or PyTorch experience is not assumed.

Syllabus: theory and practice

16 lessons · 2 hours each

Read across each row to connect a concept with its practical task. Select a lesson title for objectives, evidence to submit, and readings.

16 lessons · 32 teaching hours

Theory lessons and the corresponding practical work
LessonTheoryProject preparation

Foundations 4h · Transformers 10h · Language, vision & multimodal 8h · LLM agents 8h · Integration 2h.

Core work emphasizes calculations, tensor shapes, implementation, and observable results. Lengthy derivations, diffusion training, and advanced adaptation are optional extensions.

Preparation and two-week course design

Four individual preparation exercises

Complete these during the theory course. The tasks in the lesson table are steps within these four submissions, not sixteen separate assignments.

    Common requirements, different applications

      Two-week sequence after the core lectures

        Preparation exercises count toward the theory grade. The project grade assesses application-specific integration, evaluation, reproducibility, and individual understanding; reused preparation work is not graded twice.

        Assessment

        Separate grades for the two courses

        Theory course

        Theory course grading
        Four individual preparation exercises30%
        Short quizzes20%
        Individual open-book written exam50%

        Project course

        Project course grading
        System implementation25%
        Experiments & failure analysis25%
        Engineering & reproducibility15%
        Individual defense & live modification35%

        Theory exam: attention calculations, tensor shapes, code tracing, language–vision comparisons, and agent failure diagnosis. Course materials may be consulted; AI assistance is not permitted.

        Project grading: implementation, evaluation, and reproducibility receive a shared team score (65%). Each student earns an individual score (35%) by explaining a design decision, diagnosing a failure, and making a small live code change without AI assistance.

        AI assistance: allowed in exercises and projects with disclosure of what it helped with and how the output was verified. Students remain responsible for their submissions. The final exam, individual defense, and live modification are completed without AI assistance.
